title: Run each pane and agent session in its own systemd scope: slices, the scope decision, panes
notes:
Part 1 of 4: run each pane and agent session in its own systemd scope (cards: this, SDK sessions + tasks, stop on close, memory readout).

Why (user's measurement, 2026-11-09, ~20 sessions): RAM 27/31Gi, swap 15.4/16Gi, desktop stalled on memory 10-15% of the time, one 2-minute freeze. Dashboard is launched into one transient scope (app.slice/app-dashboard-<pid>.scope) that holds the main process and every agent child (claude, node, vitest, jest, tsc, next): 15.4G RAM, 4.4G swap, ~10 cores, all cgroup weights default, no MemoryHigh/MemoryMax. The kernel and the OOM killer cannot tell sessions apart; a 12G jest run swaps the whole desktop. Already on the laptop: VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=3 (environment.d), earlyoom tuned. Docker containers are out of scope.

This card:
1. src/main/processes/scope.ts, pure: scopedCommand({ kind, id, file, args }, support) -> { file, args }.
   - kind 'agent' (a Claude in a pane or a session, as pane.dispatch decided): systemd-run --user --scope --collect --slice=agents.slice --unit=agent-<slug>-<4 random> -p MemoryHigh=<per-scope> -p MemoryMax=<per-scope> -- file args
   - kind 'shell' (the user's own pane, nvim): same with --slice=panes.slice --unit=pane-<slug>-<4 random>, no per-scope cap.
   - support unavailable: file and args unchanged.
   - slug from the pane or session id, readable in systemd-cgtop and systemctl --user status 'agent-*'.
   The per-scope values (start: MemoryHigh=6G, MemoryMax=8G) are named constants with a decision entry; the slice values live in the unit files.
2. src/main/processes/scope-support.ts: one check at launch (systemd-run present, `systemctl --user is-system-running` or equivalent answers, Linux only), cached; on failure one log warning (log:write, #248 fields) and every spawn falls back. A unit name that collides gets one retry with a new suffix, then falls back. Never block a session from starting.
3. Slice units: on launch, write ~/.config/systemd/user/agents.slice ([Slice] CPUWeight=30, MemoryHigh=16G, MemoryMax=20G, MemorySwapMax=6G) and panes.slice (no caps) only when missing, then `systemctl --user daemon-reload`; never overwrite; the user tunes with a drop-in (agents.slice.d/override.conf). Through an action (actions-rule-1), e.g. src/main/actions/processes/install-slices.ts.
4. Spawn site: pane-shell.ts (pty.spawn inside the pane host) builds its command through scopedCommand. The pane's kind travels on the spawn request from pane.dispatch / pane.open / pane.restore. NOT hostCommand: that starts the pane host itself, one process for every pane. The pane host and screen host processes stay where they are; only what they start is scoped.
5. The scope's unit name is recorded on the pane's record (for card 3's stop and card 4's readout).
6. A guard test in the style of bypasses.test.ts: spawn( / pty.spawn( / execFile with a long-running child appear only in the files allowed to start processes (scope-aware sites plus the documented exceptions: start-app, git calls, short probes). Lower, never raise.

Constraints: Dashboard main and renderer stay out of agents.slice; processes an agent starts (Bash tools, test runners, detached dev servers) stay in its scope (--scope keeps the caller as parent, so pty and stdio work). Windows and macOS: unavailable, unchanged.

Engineering bar (user, 2026-11-09): clean, testable, readable, well engineered. Decisions in the two pure modules with tests (each kind, unavailable, collision retry, slug); the side effects (spawning, writing units, daemon-reload) thin and at the edge behind ports. No abbreviations. Files well under 600 lines.

Hand check: with 3+ sessions running tests, systemd-cgls --user shows one agent-*.scope per agent pane under agents.slice and one pane-*.scope per shell under panes.slice, and Dashboard's main process is under neither.
Docs: a new docs/processes feature folder (README, hard rules, decisions, history), docs index, panes README.

comments.body: Shipped in #253: each pane's shell runs in its own systemd scope (agent-*.scope under agents.slice, capped 6G/8G; pane-*.scope under panes.slice), slices written once at launch, unit recorded per pane and on kept shells, guard test on process starts, docs/processes.
Pull request #253 merged: Run each pane's shell in a systemd scope of its own https://github.com/naeemba/dashboard/pull/253
